$comment: A GENERATED board of the REAL Earth: the Mediterranean. Like every generated map, `commission` is the only thing anybody writes by hand and `rows`, `settlements`, `regions`, `routes` and the `plate` block are grown from it by `node tools/draw-map.mjs earth-mediterranean`. Unlike the others its land is not invented: `commission.earth` points at sampled real data (data/earth/mediterranean.samples.json, from tools/fetch-earth.mjs) and the terrain is classified from it by data/earth/classify.json. Do not hand-edit the generated parts.
name: The Mediterranean
subtitle: the sea at the middle of the world, from the Atlantic to the Euphrates, as it really is
summary: The real Mediterranean, laid onto a hex board: Iberia to Anatolia, the Alps to the Sahara, with every coast, mountain range and river where the planet put it. Built to teach geography as much as to play on: each region and a handful of places carry a note about WHY the land is the way it is.

commission.$comment: The input contract for a real-Earth region. Nothing here is invented: where the land is comes from sampled data, and what is typed is the window, the names and the lessons.
commission.why: To start the Earth line of maps: a board whose geography the real world has already worked out, so a player learns what a rain shadow, a delta, a steppe and a strait look like by playing on them. It is also the first region of a three-level scheme - Atlas, Region, Mini-map - in which this board is one window onto the planet.
commission.landmass: The real Mediterranean basin and its shores: the Iberian peninsula in the west, the Alps and the Italian peninsula in the north, the Balkans and Greece, Anatolia and the Levant in the east, and the North African coast with the edge of the Sahara in the south. The sea is the middle of the board.
commission.$terrainBudgetNote: Left empty on purpose: a real place has no budget. The tool writes the shares it measured here when it runs.
commission.$settlementNote: Real cities, placed at their real latitude and longitude. Rank is a game judgement about how much a table should make of the place, not a population count.

earth.$comment: The Earth block: what makes this map a real place and not an invented one. A map with this block has no landform anchors to grow: its land, its coasts, its mountains and its climate come from sampled real data (data/earth/*.samples.json), classified by data/earth/classify.json. Everything here is a fact about the planet - a latitude, a longitude, a river's name - and no hex is ever typed.
earth.$hexKmNote: Flat to flat, so a hex is about 17,000 square kilometres: Sicily is a hex and a half, Crete and Cyprus are about half a hex each. The board is the same 32 x 24 as every other, so its hexes print the same size and every token and sheet in the box still fits. That is the scale decision; a finer region is a second board, not smaller hexes here.

regions.name: Libya

regions.name: The Sahara

regions.name: Sicily

regions.name: Crete

regions.name: Cyprus

lessons.title: Rain shadow
lessons.text: Wet air rises over the Atlas mountains and drops its rain on the sea side. The air that comes down the far side is dry. That is why a desert sits right behind green hills.

lessons.title: A river through a desert
lessons.text: The Nile crosses a thousand kilometres of desert without a tributary. Everything green in Egypt is within reach of it.

lessons.title: Where two plates meet
lessons.text: Africa is slowly pushing north into Europe. That squeeze raised the Alps, the Apennines and the Taurus, and it feeds the volcanoes of Etna and Vesuvius.

lessons.title: A shallow sea
lessons.text: The northern Adriatic is shallow: you could nearly wade a ship into it. The shelf shows as pale water on the board; the dark water is where the sea floor drops away.

lessons.title: Narrow straits
lessons.text: The Strait of Gibraltar is under 15 km across at its narrowest, and the Bosphorus under one. At this scale they vanish, though a fleet has to pass through each one.

lessons.title: The Mediterranean climate
lessons.text: Hot dry summers and mild wet winters. Olives, vines and wheat all suit it, and so did the first cities that traded them.

lessons.title: Steppe
lessons.text: Where there is not enough rain for forest and too much for desert, grass takes over. Steppe is good for herds and for armies on horseback.

lessons.title: Deltas
lessons.text: A river slows as it meets the sea and drops the silt it carried. The land that grows from that silt is flat, fertile and often wet.

lessons.title: Oases
lessons.text: A spring in a desert makes a village possible. Siwa has been inhabited for thousands of years, and caravans plan their whole route from one oasis to the next.

lessons.title: The lowest land on Earth
lessons.text: The shore of the Dead Sea lies more than 400 metres below sea level, at the bottom of a rift valley where two plates are pulling apart.

earth.$riversNote: Five rivers, not nine: the ones whose valleys carried a civilisation. At 140 km a hex, every river on the board is a hex wide and stops a cart, so a stream that would not stop one in life is left off. The Loire, Duero, Ebro and Guadalquivir were sampled and dropped; add them back to this list and run fetch-earth.mjs if the board wants them.

plate.$note: Vector, so no long side to fall short of.

plate.$kindNote: Drawn by tools/draw-map.mjs from rows, not painted and traced. It is a build output: never hand-edited, regenerated by its tool, and safe to delete. A "drawn" plate is the opposite and the rules in docs/map/README.md are for that one.
plate.$fieldNote: Exact, because the tool chose it. On a drawn plate this is measured off the inner frame rule by eye and is the fiddliest step in the whole line.

grid.$fitNote: The same 32 x 24 as the other boards so a hex prints the same size. At the Earth scale in commission.earth.hexKm one hex is about 140 km across.

print.$comment: Sheet layouts in the same three sizes as every other board. mapWidthMm, mapHeightMm and hexAcrossFlatsMm are derived and written in by tools/build-map.mjs.

presets.name: Four sheets, A2
presets.note: Two by two, printed landscape. The working size for a table.

presets.name: Nine sheets, A1
presets.note: Three by three. A vector plate prints at this size without asking.

presets.name: One sheet, reference
presets.note: The whole board on one page, for reading rather than playing.

legend.$comment: Character to terrain id, identical to the other two boards so a board from any map reads the same in a text editor.

$rowsNote: GENERATED by tools/draw-map.mjs from commission.landform. Do not hand-edit: run the tool. On a drawn map this block is traced off the artwork instead, and hand-correcting it is expected.
$riversNote: GENERATED. Each course is the chain of hexes the water runs through, spring first, and every one of those hexes is terrain `river` in rows. Run downhill by tools/draw-map.mjs from the terrain bands and the distance inland - never hand-placed, because a hand-placed river is how you get one that starts nowhere.
